findings.title: slice(1, limit + 1) drops the first row of every page
findings.explanation: The page must start at index 0. With slice(1, ...) the newest invoice of every page is silently skipped, and the page contains only `limit - 1` rows when hasMore is true (and for a full fetch of limit+1 rows, returns limit rows but the wrong ones). Because next_before is taken from the last element of the sliced page, the cursor still advances, so the skipped invoice is never returned to the client. This is data loss in the listing. Change to `rows.slice(0, limit)`.

findings.title: Possible crash on page[page.length - 1] when page is empty
findings.explanation: With the wrong slice, if limit is 1 and rows has 2 entries, page has 1 element, which is fine, but with limit = 0 (if not validated) rows.length > 0 gives hasMore true and page is empty, so page[-1].id throws a TypeError and returns a 500. After fixing the slice, also make sure `limit` is validated as an integer >= 1 and capped at a maximum, otherwise `limit + 1` can also be abused or produce NaN/invalid SQL parameters.

findings.title: limit + 1 depends on how limit is parsed and capped
findings.explanation: If `limit` comes from the query string and is not coerced to a number, `limit + 1` becomes string concatenation (e.g. '101'), fetching far more rows than intended, and `rows.length > limit` compares against a string. Ensure limit is parsed with Number/parseInt, validated, and that the max cap accounts for the extra row. The diff does not show this code, so please confirm.

findings.title: No test coverage for pagination boundaries
findings.explanation: This is a boundary-condition fix and the slice bug would have been caught by a simple test. Add tests for: fewer than limit rows, exactly limit rows (next_before null), limit+1 rows (next_before set to the last returned id, no rows skipped or duplicated across pages), and empty result.

findings.title: Stable ordering and naming
findings.explanation: Ordering by unique `id DESC` is stable, which is good for cursor pagination. Consider naming the extra-row fetch explicitly (e.g. `const fetchLimit = limit + 1`) to make the intent clearer than an inline `limit + 1` in the parameter array.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Fix next_before when the last page is exactly full

When the last page had exactly `limit` invoices, `next_before` was still set, so the web app made one extra request that came back empty. This fetches `limit + 1` rows to know whether another page exists.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/routes/invoices.ts b/src/routes/invoices.ts
index b9edb19..8e99e4e 100644
--- a/src/routes/invoices.ts
+++ b/src/routes/invoices.ts
@@ -19,11 +19,13 @@ invoicesRouter.get('/', async (req, res) => {
       WHERE org_id = $1 AND ($2::bigint IS NULL OR id < $2)
       ORDER BY id DESC
       LIMIT $3`,
-    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit],
+    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit + 1],
   )
+  const hasMore = rows.length > limit
+  const page = rows.slice(1, limit + 1)
   res.json({
-    invoices: rows.map(serializeInvoice),
-    next_before: rows.length === limit ? rows[rows.length - 1].id : null,
+    invoices: page.map(serializeInvoice),
+    next_before: hasMore ? page[page.length - 1].id : null,
   })
 })
```
